verses.english: Linked Discourses 12.31
4. Kaḷāra the Aristocrat
What Has Come to Be
At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Tatra kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ āmantesi:
verses.english: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Sāriputta,
“Sāriputta, this was said in ‘The Way to the Far Shore’, in ‘The Questions of Ajita’:
‘There are those who have appraised the teaching,
and many kinds of trainees here.
Now you, being alert, are asked
to tell me their behavior, good fellow.’

verses.pali: Imassa nu kho, sāriputta, saṅkhittena bhāsitassa kathaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti?
verses.english: How should we see the detailed meaning of this brief statement?”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto tuṇhī ahosi.
verses.english: When he said this, Sāriputta kept silent.

verses.pali: Dutiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ āmantesi …pe…
verses.english: For a second time …

verses.pali: dutiyampi kho āyasmā sāriputto tuṇhī ahosi.
Tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ āmantesi:
verses.english: For a third time …

verses.pali: Imassa nu kho, sāriputta, saṅkhittena bhāsitassa kathaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti?
Tatiyampi kho āyasmā sāriputto tuṇhī ahosi.
verses.english: Sāriputta kept silent.
“Sāriputta, do you see that this has come to be?”
“Sir, one truly sees with right wisdom that this has come to be.

verses.pali: Bhūtamidanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā bhūtassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
verses.english: Seeing this, one is practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding what has come to be.
One truly sees with right wisdom that it originated with that as fuel.

verses.pali: Tadāhārasambhavanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā āhārasambhavassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
verses.english: Seeing this, one is practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding the fuel for its origination.

verses.pali: Tadāhāranirodhā yaṁ bhūtaṁ taṁ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
verses.english: One truly sees with right wisdom that when that fuel ceases, what has come to be is liable to cease.

verses.pali: Tadāhāranirodhā yaṁ bhūtaṁ taṁ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā nirodhadhammassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
verses.english: Seeing this, one is practicing for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding what is liable to cease.
In this way one is a trainee.
And what, sir, is one who has appraised the teaching?
Sir, one truly sees with right wisdom that this has come to be.

verses.pali: Bhūtamidanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā bhūtassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto hoti.
verses.english: Seeing this, one is freed by not grasping through disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding what has come to be.
One truly sees with right wisdom that it originated with that as fuel.

verses.pali: Tadāhārasambhavanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā āhārasambhavassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto hoti.
verses.english: Seeing this, one is freed by not grasping through disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding the fuel for its origination.

verses.pali: Tadāhāranirodhā yaṁ bhūtaṁ taṁ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
verses.english: One truly sees with right wisdom that when that fuel ceases, what has come to be is liable to cease.

verses.pali: Tadāhāranirodhā yaṁ bhūtaṁ taṁ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā nirodhadhammassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto hoti.
verses.english: Seeing this, one is freed by not grasping through disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding what is liable to cease.
In this way one has appraised the teaching.

verses.pali: Iti kho, bhante, yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ pārāyane ajitapañhe:
verses.english: Sir, regarding what was said in ‘The Way to the Far Shore’, in ‘The Questions of Ajita’:
‘There are those who have appraised the teaching,
and many kinds of trainees here.
Now you, being alert, are asked
to tell me their behavior, good fellow.’

verses.pali: Imassa khvāhaṁ, bhante, saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmī”ti.
verses.english: This is how I understand the detailed meaning of what was said in brief.”

verses.pali: “Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta, bhūtamidanti, sāriputta, yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
verses.english: “Good, good, Sāriputta!” (The Buddha repeated all of Sāriputta’s explanation, concluding:)

verses.pali: Bhūtamidanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā bhūtassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
Tadāhārasambhavanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā āhārasambhavassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
Tadāhāranirodhā yaṁ bhūtaṁ taṁ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
Tadāhāranirodhā yaṁ bhūtaṁ taṁ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā nirodhadhammassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
Bhūtamidanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā bhūtassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto hoti.
Tadāhārasambhavanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā āhārasambhavassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto hoti.
Tadāhāranirodhā yaṁ bhūtaṁ taṁ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
Tadāhāranirodhā yaṁ bhūtaṁ taṁ nirodhadhammanti yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññā disvā nirodhadhammassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimutto hoti.
Iti kho, sāriputta, yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ pārāyane ajitapañhe:
Imassa kho, sāriputta, saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti.
verses.english: This is how to understand the detailed meaning of what was said in brief.”
